questions.question: What is Brownian motion?
options: The random motion of particles suspended in a medium.
The movement of particles from high to low concentration.
The change of state from a liquid to a solid.
The chemical reaction between an acid and an alkali.

questions.question: What eventually happens to substances whose particles are free to move in a container?
options: They will settle at the bottom of the container in layers.
They will reach a random distribution throughout.
They will clump together at the center of the container.
They will escape the container even if it is tightly sealed.

questions.question: How does a higher temperature affect the particles in a gas or solution?
options: They move more quickly.
They stop moving completely.
They increase in mass.
They become tightly bonded.

questions.question: Why are suspensions not classified as solutions?
options: Because they are always made of two different liquids.
Because the solid particles can be seen and will eventually settle over time.
Because they cannot conduct electricity at room temperature.
Because they can only be formed at very high temperatures.

questions.question: What must be overcome for a solute particle to dissolve in a solvent?
options: The forces of attraction between solute particles.
The atmospheric pressure acting on the beaker.
The gravity pulling down on the solvent particles.
The electrical charge of the container walls.

questions.question: When mixing two different liquids, why might the total volume be less than expected?
options: Some particles are destroyed during the mixing process.
One type of particle may fit into the spaces between the other type.
The mass of the mixture decreases significantly.
The particles expand and push each other out of the container.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding dissolving and melting?
options: Dissolving requires a heat source, whereas melting does not.
They are both chemical reactions that form new substances.
Dissolving is not the same as melting, but both are physical processes.
Melting involves a solvent, while dissolving only involves one substance.

questions.question: To ensure that an investigation's method is high-quality, how should it be written?
options: Using complex language that only expert scientists can understand.
So that it is both repeatable and reproducible.
Containing opinions on what the results should have been.
Without mentioning any specific equipment or quantities.

questions.question: How is a solution formed?
options: When an insoluble solid settles at the bottom of a liquid.
When a soluble solid dissolves in an appropriate solvent.
When two gases react chemically to produce a new gas.
When a liquid turns into a gas through boiling.

questions.question: If 5 grams of salt is completely dissolved in 100 grams of water, what is the total mass of the mixture?
options: Exactly 105 grams, because mass is conserved.
Less than 100 grams, because some salt is lost during dissolving.
Exactly 100 grams, because the salt occupies the spaces between water particles.
More than 105 grams, because dissolving increases the mass of individual particles.

questions.question: Which of these is a characteristic of a pure material?
options: It melts and boils over a wide range of temperatures.
It has a fixed melting point and boiling point.
It is made of at least three different types of substances.
Its properties change every time it is heated.

questions.question: What effect do impurities have on the melting and boiling points of a material?
options: They keep the melting and boiling points exactly the same.
They change the melting and boiling point of the material.
They make the material unable to ever melt or boil.
They cause the material to melt and boil at a single, higher fixed temperature.

questions.question: At a given temperature, which of the following is true about dissolving a solute in a solvent?
options: An infinite amount of solute can always be dissolved.
There is a limit to how much solute can dissolve in a solvent.
Solutes can only dissolve if the solvent is boiling.
The solute will always float on top of the solvent.

questions.question: What can happen to dissolved solutes as a solution cools down?
options: They may become insoluble and precipitate out.
They will always evaporate into the air.
They turn into a completely new chemical element.
They increase the volume of the liquid.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of factors can affect the solubility of a substance?
options: Only the shape of the beaker and the time of day.
The size of the solute pieces, the choice of solvent, or the temperature of the solvent.
Only the color of the solute and the room's humidity.
The volume of the container and the air pressure.

questions.question: What is the independent variable in a scientific investigation?
options: The factor that is kept the same to ensure a fair test.
The factor that is observed or measured to see the effect.
The factor that is changed in the investigation.
The piece of equipment used to record the data.

questions.question: What is done in a fair test to ensure we know which variable made a difference to the results?
options: All variables are changed at the same time.
No variables are allowed to change at all.
Only the variable being tested is changed.
Only the control variables are changed during the experiment.
